record.original_question: An r-graph is an r-regular graph G such that every odd vertex set X subseteq V(G) is joined to its complement by at least r edges. Such a graph is poorly matchable if any two of its perfect matchings intersect. Is there a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph?

evidence.quote: An r-graph is an r-regular graph G such that every odd set X subseteq V (G) is connected by at least r edges to its complement V (G) \ X. An r-graph is poorly matchable if any two of its perfect matchings intersect.
Problem 5.2 Is there a poorly matchable 5-edge-connected 5-graph?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Define an r-graph (for a positive integer r) to be an r-regular multigraph G on a finite even-order vertex set such that for every odd-cardinality vertex subset X ⊆ V(G), the number of edges with one endpoint in X and the other in V(G)∖X is at least r. A perfect matching of G is a set of edges that covers every vertex exactly once; by parity and the r-graph condition, every r-graph has perfect matchings. Call an r-graph poorly matchable if any two of its perfect matchings share at least one edge.

Question: Does there exist a 5-graph G that is 5-edge-connected (i.e., every edge cut of G has at least 5 edges) and poorly matchable?
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on poorly matchable r-graphs and pairwise disjoint perfect matchings indicates that all known poorly matchable r-graphs contain a 4-edge-cut, and no 5-edge-connected poorly matchable 5-graph is known. The problem appears to be open.

status_evidence.title: The hardness of recognising poorly matchable graphs and the hunting of the d-snark
status_evidence.snippet: All known poorly matchable r-graphs have a 4-edge-cut; no 5-edge-connected poorly matchable r-graph is known.
status_evidence.claim: Existence of a 5-edge-connected poorly matchable 5-graph is posed as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Pairwise Disjoint Perfect Matchings in r-Edge-Connected r-Regular Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies disjoint perfect matchings in r-edge-connected r-regular graphs, with r=5 being a notable open case.
status_evidence.claim: The 5-edge-connected case for 5-regular graphs remains open in the related disjoint-matchings problem.
